summary: Correct the first supporting whistling reference from verse 5 to verse 4
rationale: The main quotation is correctly at 116/17. Of the additional references, 96/5 contains greetings and no whistling verb; the immediately preceding 96/4 has gmašrəq in the pipe-smoking scene. Verse 96/18 has kmašrəq in the same scene and remains valid. These are supporting attestations, not an alternative location for the whole 116/17 quotation.

summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1 in Preterit (59/53)

data.turoyo: Li kurfo mašraqla, aṯən ak kurfe šaʕuṯe di arʕo kulle.
data.translation: Die Schlange zischte; da kamen alle gelben Schlangen der Erde herbei.

rationale: New III Preterit box; feminine animal agent and summons context.

data.turoyo: <...> Bi poṯo du qalač kito ḥa yatiwo ʕal u kursi, kile u pipayḏe b feme w maḥatle raġle ʕal raġlo w kale kwitkwit diḏe, u pipayḏe b feme gmašrəq w kšote u pipayḏe.
data.translation: <...> auf dem Abhand des Grünhangs sitzt einer auf dem Stuhle, mit der Pfeife im Maul und mit übergeschlagenen Beinen, pfeift vergnügt vor sich hin und raucht seine Pfeife. <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; human whistling in a pipe-smoking scene, distinct from instrument playing.

data.turoyo: Hani, ab baqore w ar ruʕye, u yawmo kule komašərqi bu mašruqo. Koyəlfi aʕle ġalabe basimo, kodayqi aʕle.
data.translation: Diese Rinder- und Ziegenhirten blasen den ganzen Tag auf der Flöte. Sie lernen sehr schön darauf zu spielen.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; plural playing with explicit b- instrument.

data.turoyo: <...> Yatuno, mašraqno ʕal u mašruqayḏi, koḥozeno qumi, kut mede koroməš. <...>
data.translation: <...> Ich setzte mich und blies auf meiner Flöte, da sah ich vor mir etwas sich bewegen. <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum cell reaches five; 1sg unprefixed form with ʕal instrument in past narrative.

summary: All nine records checked. New Preterit examples belong to III, with mašraqla retaining l-agent morphology despite an otherwise intransitive sound event.
Human whistling and flute playing both remain inherited sense1. Instrument coding alternates b- and ʕal; context identifies the instrument, not the prefix alone.
The supplied Infinitiv bird-chirping example and wind example already establish nonhuman sound/air participants; snake calls fit an extension.
A partial alignment warning at 116/24 prevents quotation of that translation. No later stone action or new verb is inferred.
kwitkwit is adjacent to the whistling predicate but is not demonstrated to form an idiom with šrq; no speculative collocation is added.
Check the German extra dialogue at 59/55 and later stone clause in the translation of 116/24 against the edition; neither is copied into added examples.
Check the legacy parallel 96/5 against supplied piper scene 96/4 before changing the existing reference.
Is kwitkwit diḏe an independent expression? It is not evidence of a fixed šrq construction.
Snake hissing/whistling summons other snakes; animal subject does not independently warrant a new sense.
